strings.patient_bundles.patient_nishikawa_natsuk: Natsuki Nishikawa
“Hospitalization...? Doctor, do you think my condition is serious? Please tell me the reason directly. I-I want to know the worst-case possibility first.”
“...All right, I'll be admitted. I'll request leave from school myself. Only, once the test results come back, please don't hide anything from me, okay?”
“Wait a minute! The surgery you mentioned earlier isn't the same as what you're saying now, is it? Don't assume I can't understand anything just because I'm nervous—please double-check it first!”
“...Now I understand. Thank you for explaining the reason. Until the results are out, I'll try my best not to jump to conclusions on my own.”
“Just ‘following standard procedure’? Doctor, I didn't come here to be brushed off. At least tell me why this step is necessary!”
“It's not that I don't trust you... I'm just terrified of hearing bad news. Could you tell me one more time who will be staying here with me next?”
“General anesthesia... I won't know anything at all until I wake up, right?... All right. Then please tell me the results the very moment I wake up.”
“Epidural anesthesia? My mind stays awake while my body can't move... I understand the principle, but just imagining it is a bit hard to bear.”
“Local anesthesia... I'll still be able to speak, right? If I feel anything distinct inside, I'll report it immediately, so please make sure you listen.”
“No anesthesia at all?!... Are you serious? I push myself to endure pressure every single day, but that doesn't mean I can endure a scalpel!”
“...I'll count my breaths. I'll stop thinking about the exams for now... Doctor, please, don't let me fall asleep with a head full of unanswered questions.”
“It hurts... it really hurts! I know I have to cooperate, but you can't just tell me to tough it out! Please listen to where I can't bear it first!”
“D-don't hold me down all at once! I know I mustn't move, but I don't have any anesthesia... Just thinking about the pain coming next makes my body flinch on its own!”
“I'll hold this posture... Ngh, that just pulled inside! Don't say I'm overreacting—I really can still feel it there!”
“I really can't put any strength into my legs at all... I know someone is helping hold me in place, but this sensation makes me so uneasy. Please tell me before adjusting my position.”
“I already said I'll cooperate... W-wait! The scalpel is right there... No! Please don't bring it down yet, I'm really terrified...!”
“...Have you already made the cut? There isn't the sharp pain I imagined, yet knowing the blade is cutting into my body... ugh, why is my heart beating so fast...”
“Hiss—! The outside feels numb, but the pulling sensation inside is so clear! Doctor, please check again—is it really supposed to feel like this?”
“Aaah—!! It hurts! You really cut me open! Wait, wait a second! I can't hold it in... please stop for a moment!”
“...Did you stop? Thank you... please let me catch my breath. A second ago I even forgot what I was trying to say.”
“I know, I mustn't move... I'll try! But please don't just give orders—I need to know how much longer this will take!”
“We have to keep going, huh... All right. I'll listen to you, but if I cry out again, please don't think I'm talking back on purpose.”
“Which step are we on now?... Thank you. At least when I hear the progress, I don't keep assuming the worst.”
“Doctor... could you look at me while you speak? I'm not trying to interrupt—I just want to be sure everyone is still paying attention to my condition.”
“Why did it suddenly go so quiet? Did something go wrong?... Doctor, please answer me, my mind is racing again!”
“It's almost over...? Really?... Thank goodness. I'm sorry I sounded so sharp earlier. Thank you all for answering my questions the whole time.”
“Follow your breathing... okay, one, two... I can do this. Please keep talking—it's much less scary when I can hear your voice.”
“...Please let me be quiet for a little while. I'm not angry with you... I'm just relieved I finally don't have to keep picturing terrible outcomes.”
“An enema too...? I know it's preoperative preparation, but I didn't expect this step. Could you explain why it's necessary first?”
“U-understood. I'll cooperate... just please don't leave me guessing while you get things ready. Knowing clearly in advance is much better.”
“Wait, I didn't say I wouldn't do it! I'm just a bit embarrassed... Could you give me a moment to prepare myself mentally?”
“No enema needed this time?... Okay. That's decided based on the surgical procedure, right? For a moment I thought you had skipped a step by mistake.”
“Phew... so we can skip that one. Sorry, yesterday I already ran through all the most embarrassing preparation steps in my head.”
“Skin prep... which areas need to be shaved?... Please don't think I'm asking too many questions, I just want to know the range beforehand.”
“You have to shave down there too?! I know it's required for the surgery... but this is completely different from a school health checkup!”
“Okay, I won't move around... but please draw the curtain closed first. The more I try to act unbothered, the hotter my face feels.”
“No skin prep needed?... I see. Here I was wondering if part of the preoperative preparation had been left out.”
“It's really not required?... All right, then I won't press further. Honestly, I was just trying to figure out how to admit that I was embarrassed.”
“All my hair has to be tucked inside... Okay. Putting on this cap suddenly makes it feel real that I'm about to be wheeled into the operating room.”
“I don't look like my usual self at all in the mirror... Never mind, that's not what matters right now. What comes next?”
“Arms placed here, body centered without leaning... Got it. Please have just one person give the instructions—too many voices at once will make me panic.”
“Do I have to be positioned like this...? I know you aren't doing it to make things hard for me, but being in front of so many people feels really uncomfortable.”
“Wait—could you say a word before holding me to adjust my posture? I'll cooperate, so you don't need to treat me like I can't understand.”
“No anesthesia at all, and I still have to hold this position the entire time?... I know I mustn't move, but what happens when it really starts hurting?”
“I'll try my best not to struggle... but just thinking about being cut open in a moment makes my legs tremble uncontrollably.”
“P-please make sure the restraints are secure. I'm not trying to act tough... I'm afraid I won't be able to control myself once it starts.”
“Urinary catheterization has to be done too?... I know it's medical preparation. Just please explain clearly what needs to be done first...”
“Miss Nurse, please wait a second... I'm really embarrassed. Could you ask the others nearby not to look this way for now?”
“Hiss...! I am trying to relax. You don't have to keep saying ‘don't be nervous’—the more I hear it, the more tense I get...”
“Having a catheter put in without any anesthesia... I know it isn't the incision itself, but asking me to relax at a time like this is just too hard.”
“P-please tell me before you start! I don't want to jerk away... but right now I'm too scared to even think about the next step.”
“Is this step finished...? I shouldn't be using up all my fear on this when the scalpel is still ahead... ah, there I go overthinking again.”
“So cold... that's the antiseptic, right? Yes, I understand. Does this mean the operation is about to begin for real...?”
“So the disinfection area is this wide... I know there's a reason for it, but lying here like this makes me feel completely helpless.”
“Wait—is this the final preparation before the incision? I'm wide awake, and I don't have any anesthesia at all...!”
“It's freezing... I know this is only disinfection, yet I'm already imagining what it's going to feel like when the blade comes down...”
“P-please don't go silent all of a sudden! I'm not asking questions to stall—I'm genuinely terrified out of my wits!”
“This line is the planned incision?... Understood. Seeing it drawn on my own body feels completely different from just hearing the name of the procedure.”
“I know you've already double-checked... but could you confirm for me one more time that the marked position is exact?”
“With no anesthesia at all... this line is really where you're about to cut?... I can't bear to look.”
“Don't bring the scalpel over so fast! I'm not saying I want to cancel... it's just that seeing the mark on my skin makes the fear inside me almost overwhelming.”
“Doctor, please answer me one thing first... You will warn me right before the blade touches my skin, won't you?”
Doctor, I originally wanted to wait until this week's classes were over before coming in... but what's wrong with my body is: {line}
I'll explain in chronological order—the most obvious problem is: {line}. Please listen carefully, I'm not exaggerating.
There's one more thing I mustn't leave out: {line}. I know I sound tense, but I'm afraid missing a detail could affect your diagnosis.

My name is Natsuki Nishikawa. I'm studying for entrance exams at a highly competitive cram school, and I often spend all weekend studying too. Lately, whenever anything feels even slightly off with my body, my mind jumps straight to the worst possible outcome... I've even had nightmares about being told I have cancer. Doctor, please don't just chalk all my symptoms up to exam stress.
Outpatient Examination of Natsuki Nishikawa
“For this examination... I have to take off all my clothes? Wait—I'm not saying I won't cooperate! Just please tell me first how much you need to examine, okay?”
“We're holding off on this examination for now?... That's a relief. Still, if it's genuinely necessary, please don't skip it just because I'm nervous.”
“I-I got it, I'll cooperate! But Doctor, is it really that hard to explain the scope of the examination first?... Sorry, I lost my composure a little.”
“Thank you for explaining first... I'll do as you say. Still, having someone look at my body for an exam is much more embarrassing than I imagined.”
“The more you pressure me like that, the more scared I get!... I'm not trying to refuse a necessary exam—just please don't treat my questions like I'm talking back on purpose.”
Preoperative Arrangements for Natsuki Nishikawa

“Dr. Sakaguchi... the surgery is today, isn't it? I've already notified my school. Could you go over the schedule clearly for me once more?... I'm not trying to give you a hard time; I'm just afraid I missed something important.”

“I want to ask in detail. Once I'm on the operating table later, from positioning and disinfection to making the incision, how exactly will each step proceed?... If you only tell me ‘don't worry,’ my mind will jump straight to the worst-case scenario.”

At first, Natsuki listens as though taking notes on key points before an exam, trying hard to memorize every step the medical staff explain. Yet when the explanation reaches field exposure, the incision, and the subsequent operative steps, her eager questioning suddenly grows quiet. What sounded like steps on paper a moment ago is about to happen to her own body; she clutches the corner of the blanket tighter, unable to stop picturing the worst.
